prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital medication dispensing/returns; oversight, traceability, accountability.
Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer.
Morrowglass receives authorized clinical-system orders; timestamps/validates fields, identifiers, codes, quantities, destinations; routes review; reports status; flags missing/duplicate/conflicting records; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Unresolved discrepancies block preparation; dispensing requires completed checks/authorization.
Juniper displays orders/results, supports final verification, audits decisions/status. Clinical Pharmacist checks appropriateness/doses/allergies/interactions, approves exceptions via Dose Exception Review Slip, assesses excursion/storage/delay suitability. Copperfield prepares approved medications, investigates/escalates discrepancies, obtains clarification, checks packaging/identity/lot/expiry/cold-chain limits; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card; reverifies delayed capsule contents/order identifiers before retry.
Cinderwake prepares authorized eligible orders, logs handling, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Bluejay maintains approved refrigeration, continuously timestamps temperatures, reports excursions/connectivity loss; retain duration/extent records; segregate affected stock pending authorized disposition.
Medication Safety Officer reviews trends/procedures, produces Diversion Review Packet. Tallowmere records returns, produces Return Bin Audit Label; segregates pending disposition.
East Tube Dispatch Console/West Tube Dispatch Console control authorized routing. East monitors movement/logs route/timing/status; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket for route failure/timeout. Pneumatic Tube Network transports compatible deliveries. Dispatch personnel hold affected capsules/block faulty routes; Operations staff coordinate approved alternatives/wards. Segments remain unavailable until safety testing; resumption requires checks/operations authorization. Hospital Courier handles unavailable/unsuitable automated transport.
Larkspur confirms continuing need/contingencies. Charge Nurse coordinates readiness/escalation, communicates delays/workarounds, sends Cabinet Downtime Notice; confirms notification before restoration. Ward contingency requires authorized alternative/accountability; access requires authorization/patient-care/cabinet controls. North Ward Cabinet Controller/South Ward Cabinet Controller report availability/block Out of Service dispensing.
Stonewake recovers equipment, inspects tube hardware/switches/sensors, verifies repaired cabinets. IT Operations Specialist monitors connectivity/availability, checks interfaces/logs/controller/application health. Technical staff document faults/corrections/verification.

New part:
S072: A cabinet remains unavailable until its controller reports Ready for Dispense and required operational checks are complete.
S073: Operations closes the interruption only after staff confirm that dispensing and delivery workflows are functioning as intended.
S074: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
S075: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
S076: The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
S077: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
S078: The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
S079: The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
S080: The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
S081: The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
S082: A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
S083: The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
S084: Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
S085: The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
S086: Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
S087: Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
S088: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
S089: At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
S090: The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
S091: The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
S092: The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
S093: The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
S094: The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
